decisions.reason: The source adds a light-sensor I2C connector to the integrated-board variant; it does not change the separate sensor board's established connector matrix.
A light-sensor I2C connector for backlight sensing does not change the e-paper backlight's LED supply, switching, PWM, or electrical requirements.
Including an I2C light-sensor connector does not establish the sensor's logic voltage or alter the existing level-shifting policy.
The added light-sensor I2C connector is unrelated to the SPS30 SEL connection and I2C operating mode.
The integrated-board light-sensor connector does not affect the panel reset connector or its electrical action.
The light-sensor I2C connector is distinct from the PIR input interface and does not change its state.
Adding a light-sensor I2C connector does not alter the panel button or switch connectors and GPIO assignments.
The light-sensor I2C addition does not change the capacitive-touch interfaces or their GPIO assignments.
A light sensor used for backlight control is distinct from the addressable LED power and data interface.
The integrated-board light-sensor connector does not change the separate addressable LED array board.
The light-sensor I2C connector has no effect on the passive buzzer interface or selected buzzer.

The source adds a connector within the already established integrated-board variant but does not change the variant architecture, interboard-connector policy, functionality-retention goal, or cost objective.
